data.content_ref: inline:{"analogy":null,"claim":"A test constrains its subject when the test is part of the subject's build system, and the 3-of-26 result is the number of mutations whose effects were absorbed by the build system's own error handling before the test could observe them.","counterconditions":[{"case":"If the lost mutation was in the subject's core logic and not in the build system, then the build-system mechanism is wrong.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"If the build system's error handling is identical across all 26 mutations, then the distribution cannot be explained by build-system differences.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"If re-running the test without the build system's error handling still loses the same mutation, then the constraint is not from the build system.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"}],"definitions":[],"derivation":[],"formalization_refs":[],"mechanism":"The compile.py mutation lost under shown-to-fail-first installation was not a mutation in the subject's logic but in the build system's error path. The build system's error handling (the 'shown-to-fail-first' installation) already contained logic that masked the mutation's effect. The test then described the build system's masked state, not the subject's original behavior. The 3-of-26 distribution reflects the number of mutations that were in code paths where the build system's error handling ran before the test's guards.","premises":[],"schema":"deepreason-reasoning-envelope-v1","scope":{"covers":[],"excludes":[]},"simulation_refs":[],"uncertainties":[]}
